what_its_for: Imatinib is a cancer medicine used to treat certain types of leukemia (blood cancer), including chronic myeloid leukemia (CML) and acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL). It is also used for some stomach and intestinal tumors called gastrointestinal stromal tumors (GIST), as well as other rare cancers. It works by blocking abnormal proteins that tell cancer cells to grow and multiply.
how_to_take: Take imatinib by mouth with a full glass of water (at least 8 ounces). Always take it WITH food and a large glass of water to help protect your stomach. Swallow the tablets whole — do not crush or chew them. If you have trouble swallowing, you may dissolve the tablet in a glass of water or apple juice, stir well, and drink right away. Take it at the same time every day to keep the medicine working evenly in your body.
dosing: Your doctor will decide your exact dose based on your condition, weight, and other medicines you take. Common adult doses range from 400 mg to 800 mg once daily, or sometimes split into two doses per day. For children, the dose is based on body weight. Never change your dose on your own — always follow your doctor's instructions exactly.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember on the SAME day. If it is already the next day, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time. Do NOT take two doses in one day to make up for a missed one. If you are unsure what to do, call your doctor or pharmacist.
storage: Store imatinib tablets at room temperature between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Keep the medicine in its original container with the cap tightly closed. Keep it away from heat, direct light, and moisture — do NOT store it in the bathroom. Keep all medicines safely out of reach of children and pets. Do not use the medicine after the expiration date printed on the package.
what_to_avoid: Avoid grapefruit and grapefruit juice while taking imatinib, as it can increase the amount of medicine in your blood to unsafe levels. Do not take St. John's Wort (an herbal supplement) as it can make imatinib less effective. Avoid taking acetaminophen (Tylenol) in large amounts or for long periods without talking to your doctor. Tell your doctor or pharmacist about ALL medicines, vitamins, and supplements you take, including blood thinners, antifungals, seizure medicines, and cholesterol medicines, as many drugs can interact with imatinib. Avoid getting pregnant while taking this medicine — use reliable birth control during treatment and for some time after stopping.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: sudden or severe weight gain or swelling in your hands, feet, or face; difficulty breathing or shortness of breath; chest pain; severe nausea, vomiting, or stomach pain; yellowing of your skin or eyes (signs of liver problems); black, tarry, or bloody stools; unusual bruising or bleeding; high fever or signs of infection (chills, sore throat); severe skin rash or blistering; vision changes; or if you feel very weak or faint. Also call your doctor if you develop any new or worsening symptoms.
when_it_works: Imatinib starts working in your body right away, but it may take several weeks to months before you notice improvements or before your doctor sees changes in your lab results or scans. Most patients see meaningful results within 3 to 6 months of starting treatment. It is very important to keep taking this medicine every day, even if you feel well, because stopping it can allow the cancer to come back. Your doctor will monitor your progress with regular blood tests and check-ups.
special_populations: Pregnancy: Do NOT take imatinib if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. It can harm an unborn baby. Use effective birth control during treatment and discuss options with your doctor. Breastfeeding: Do not breastfeed while taking this medicine as it passes into breast milk and may harm a nursing baby. Children: Imatinib can be used in children and teenagers; the dose is calculated based on body weight. Children may experience slower growth while on this medicine — their doctor will monitor this. Older adults (65+): Older patients may be more sensitive to side effects such as swelling and fluid retention and should be monitored closely. Kidney or liver problems: Your dose may need to be adjusted if you have kidney or liver disease — make sure your doctor knows your full medical history.
